response.sql: WITH patient_averages AS (SELECT p.ID, p.SEX, AVG(l.ALB - l.TP) AS alb_tp, AVG(l.APTT - l.PT) AS aptt_pt FROM Laboratory AS l JOIN Patient AS p ON p.ID = l.ID GROUP BY p.ID, p.SEX), sex_averages AS (SELECT SEX, AVG(alb_tp) AS alb_tp, AVG(aptt_pt) AS aptt_pt FROM patient_averages GROUP BY SEX), overall_mean AS (SELECT AVG(aptt_pt) AS mean_aptt_pt FROM sex_averages) SELECT AVG(s.alb_tp) AS avg_alb_tp, AVG(s.aptt_pt) AS avg_aptt_pt, AVG(s.aptt_pt - m.mean_aptt_pt) AS avg_excess_aptt_pt FROM sex_averages AS s CROSS JOIN overall_mean AS m WHERE s.aptt_pt > m.mean_aptt_pt;

assumptions.assumption: Each patient’s figure is the average of row-by-row differences, so a lab record contributes only when both values are present.

alternatives.interpretation: Subtract each patient’s separately calculated column averages; each average then uses all available values in its column.
